title: Choose the report's structure
question: Same Site Drawing Set look. Pick how a buyer or bank on a phone gets from 'what can I pay against?' to the frames that prove it.

options.label: Open items first
options.lineage: a site snag list, what's left to close before handover
options.thesis: The report opens on what is not yet proven and exactly what clears each item; everything verified follows as a checked appendix with its frames.
options.viewport: 9 of 12 windows verified, 3 still open; then the two open items (Bedroom 2 Short 2 with its query letter, Kitchen Not seen yet with its 5-second request), then a collapsed Verified row.
options.risk: Leading with what's open can read as bad news; the copy must keep 'what clears it' beside every item.

raised.raise: Every bar is exact: a segment per window, so the open part is measured, never decorative.
A stepped room index down the edge shows the report's whole extent and where you are in it.
Outcome colours become a strict system: one colour, one pattern, one meaning, everywhere on the page.
When a clip clears a room, its count and stamp change in place where the reader is already looking.

options.label: Plan-first sheet
options.lineage: today's report, rebuilt around the drawing
options.thesis: The blueprint plan is the report: each room's tile carries its count and stamp, and tapping one opens its frames and sources below.
options.viewport: The answer line on top, then the plan filling the phone's width with five room tiles, Bedroom 2 selected; its evidence starts below the fold.
options.risk: Familiar from today's screen; a buyer still has to tap rooms to learn what's open.

options.label: The marked-up letter
options.lineage: a checked demand letter, stamped in the margin
options.thesis: The report is the demand letter itself: each claimed line carries its stamp in the margin, and tapping a line opens its rooms and frames beneath it.
options.viewport: The letter's head (Flat 302, Stage 6), then 'Windows complete: 12' highlighted with 9 · 2 · 1 stamped beside it, opened to show its rooms; doors and plaster lines below.
options.risk: Reads as a document first; the plan and 3D become secondary, opened from a line.

options.label: Claim coupons
options.lineage: a ticket wallet, fused into the drawing set
options.thesis: Each claim is a perforated coupon: the body shows what's verified with its frames, the stub carries what's still open and what clears it.
options.viewport: A stack of coupons: Windows (9 of 12, stub: Short 2 · Not seen yet 1), Doors (4 of 5), Plaster (not checked), each coupon square-cornered with a perforated stub.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: buyers know a coupon you release; it maps onto stage payments. Holds identification, narrower on clarity for per-room evidence.
options.risk: Perforations can turn decorative; they have to separate 'proven' from 'open', nothing else.

options.label: Evidence wall
options.lineage: a streaming catalogue's rows, fused into the drawing set
options.thesis: One row per room, one tile per counted window with its outline; a missing window is an empty hatched tile, so the evidence is the count.
options.viewport: The answer line, then rows: Living Room (3 outlined tiles), Bedroom 2 (2 outlined, 2 hatched empty), Kitchen (1 hatched with a 5-second request).
options.case: Fuses cleanly: everyone reads a row of tiles; seeing the gaps beats reading a number. Strong on clarity, narrower on bank-style auditability.
options.risk: Many frames on a phone over slow data; tiles must load light and the plan must stay reachable.

options.label: Labanotation score
options.thesis: The report as a vertical score read upward.
options.viewport: A centre staff with shaded blocks per room.
options.case: Declined: buyers and banks can't read a notation they've never seen.

options.label: Acetate manual
options.thesis: Evidence on acetate leaves over tabbed dividers.
options.viewport: A tabbed manual open at a room.
options.case: Declined: layered acetate and shadow fight the flat drawing set.
options.risk: A costume of a different object.
options.kept: A stepped index showing the report's extent.

options.label: Transit diagram
options.thesis: Items as coloured lines, rooms as stations.
options.viewport: Window and door lines meeting at room stations.
options.case: Declined: a route map implies travel and order that rooms don't have.
options.kept: Outcome colours as a strict system.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: The report as a departure board of claims.
options.viewport: Rows of claims flipping to their status.
options.case: Declined: a board hides the frames, and frames are the evidence.
options.kept: Counts change in place when a clip lands.
